source_text: Non est distinctio: omnes enim peccaverunt et egent gloria Dei. Iustitia Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes qui credunt — non ex operibus legis, gratis per redemptionem quae est in Christo Iesu.
thought_title: No distinction: all have sinned and need God's glory
orientation: Origen is quoting Paul's words from Romans 3 about the universal state of sin and the righteousness of God given through faith in Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Not is [there] distinction: all [people] for have sinned and [they] lack [the] glory of God. [The] justice of God through [the] faith of Jesus Christ into all [people] who believe — not from [the] works of [the] law, freely through [the] redemption which is in Christ Jesus.

choices.why: The Latin egeo with genitive means to lack or be in need of something; 'lack' preserves the sense of deprivation rather than a mere desire.
rejected: fall short of the glory of God

choices.why: The genitive 'Iesu Christi' is ambiguous in Latin; rendering it as 'of Jesus Christ' keeps the literal genitive without resolving whether it is faith in Christ or Christ's own faithfulness.
rejected: through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ

choices.why: The adverb gratis means without payment or cost; 'freely' captures the gratuitous character of the redemption.
The Latin redemptio means a buying back or release by payment; 'redemption' is the standard literal rendering.

bible_refs.note: Non est distinctio: omnes enim peccaverunt et egent gloria Dei. Iustitia Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes qui credunt — non ex operibus legis, gratis per redemptionem quae est in Christo Iesu.

pass_b_english: There is no distinction: all have sinned and lack the glory of God. God's righteousness comes through faith of Jesus Christ to all who believe—not from works of the law, but freely through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus (Romans 3:22-24).

last_rejected.why: Genitive is ambiguous: subjective (Christ's faith) or objective (faith in Christ). 'Faith of Jesus Christ' wrongly suggests Christ's own faith.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Faith of Jesus Christ' is a literal rendering of 'fidem Iesu Christi'; ambiguity is preserved, not changed.

last_rejected.why: 'Gratis' means 'freely/by grace,' but 'freely' alone loses the technical sense of grace central to Paul's argument.
last_rejected.fix: by grace, freely, through the redemption
last_rejected.ruling: 'Gratis' means 'freely'; 'freely' is within normal range. No meaning lost; 'grace' is interpretive, not required.
